summary: This is a supplier-friendly services agreement. Acting for the Customer, the main risks are a very short payment period with a high late-payment rate, a liability cap that protects only the Supplier, an uncapped Customer indemnity, and a right for the Supplier to use Customer data for its own products. The governing-law clause lets the Supplier change the law at will.

issues.title: Payment terms and late interest
issues.explanation: Seven days to pay is unusually short, and 5% interest per month is well above usual commercial rates.
issues.recommendation: Move to 30 days and a moderate late-payment rate.

issues.title: Long initial term
issues.explanation: A 36-month first term locks the Customer in before the service has proved itself.

issues.title: One-sided liability cap
issues.explanation: The Supplier's liability is capped at one month of fees, while the Customer's liability is unlimited.
issues.recommendation: Make the cap mutual and set it at twelve months of fees.

issues.title: Uncapped Customer indemnity
issues.explanation: The Customer indemnifies all losses of any kind, even those caused by the Supplier.
issues.recommendation: Limit the indemnity to losses caused by the Customer's breach, subject to the cap.

issues.title: Use of Customer data
issues.explanation: The Supplier may use Customer data for any purpose, including training its own products.
issues.recommendation: Limit use to providing the Services.

issues.title: Governing law chosen by one party
issues.explanation: The Supplier can choose and change the governing law from time to time, so the Customer cannot know which law applies.
issues.recommendation: Fix one agreed governing law now.

edits.comment: Seven days is unusually short. Thirty days is a common commercial standard.
5% a month is far above usual late-payment rates.
A shorter first term lets the Customer test the service before a long commitment.

edits.find: the fees paid in the one (1) month
edits.replace: the fees paid in the twelve (12) months
edits.comment: One month of fees gives the Customer almost no remedy.

edits.replace: The same cap applies to the Customer.
edits.comment: The cap should protect both parties equally.

edits.find: all losses of any kind arising in connection with this Agreement
edits.replace: losses caused by the Customer’s breach of this Agreement, subject to clause 4
edits.comment: The Customer should not cover losses the Supplier causes.

edits.comment: One fixed governing law, agreed by both parties.
